reading.body:
Digital Crossroad's DX-1 campus in Hammond, Indiana publishes 20 MW of critical IT load capacity, making it the largest facility by announced power in a state where only two of six mapped data centers publish capacity figures. The facility occupies 105,000 square feet of total building space with over 72,000 square feet available as data hall. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this 20 MW of critical load translates to roughly 500 racks as an assumption about potential utilization.

The campus is certified to ISO 27001 for information security management and SOC 2 for service organization controls. Uptime Institute Tier III concurrently maintainable status, self-reported, qualifies the facility for maintenance of IT systems without downtime.

The operator reserves 100 plus MW of substation capacity on site, indicating a build envelope for future expansion beyond the currently published 20 MW critical load. This ratio of announced to reserved capacity suggests DX-1 is in an early phase of deployment relative to its infrastructure envelope. No published pricing or tenant roster is available.
